No leaderboard code is submitted. The strongest finite conclusion is a complete-cloud obstruction for Ta-Shma amplification.

For a possible sparse successor, fix explicit base labels `Z:[N_1]→F_2^r` and a search-free map `Path:{0,1}^30→{valid path descriptors}`. If path `q` visits `v_{q,0},…,v_{q,ell_q}`, define its column by `g_q=⊕_h Z(v_{q,h})`. A qualifying rank-1040 balanced core must prove, simultaneously for every nonzero `x∈F_2^1040`,

`|Σ_q (-1)^{<x,g_q>}|≤2^21`.

It may then append the all-one row to obtain dimension 1041. No such path family or character-sum proof is presently known.

distance_audit: The immutable distance is `D=2^29−2^20=535,822,336`, and the signed-sum allowance is `T=n−2D=2^21`.
The sufficient two-sided bias is `tau=T/n=1/512=2^-9`; the campaign's `2^-10` is the distance deficit, not the Fourier-bias parameter.
A `tau`-balanced rank-r core has all nonzero weights in `[D,n−D]`. It excludes the all-one word, so adjoining that word gives a rank-`r+1` code of minimum distance at least `D`.
No new code or minimum distance is claimed in this obstruction result.
explicitness_audit: Ta-Shma's complete cloud is deterministically indexed, and its full matrix can be emitted in polynomial time. Its failure here is finite length and certificate strength, not computability.

The asymptotic `epsilon^{2+o(1)}` rate cannot certify this finite target: its hidden constants are unavailable, and the paper's near-optimal parameter branch fails its stated prerequisite at `epsilon=1/512`.
A sparse replacement must provide a structural polynomial-time `Path(q)` indexer; canonical exhaustive search, conditional averaging over all completions, and finite lookup are inadmissible.
The sparse proof must control every nonzero character simultaneously and establish rank. An expectation for each character or the complete-cloud norm bound does not suffice.
No validator or dashboard build was run because this is an obstruction handoff, not a publication candidate.

generator_matrix.algorithm: No candidate matrix is asserted. For a complete-cloud audit, enumerate all start-state/instruction tuples instead of `Path(q)`.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: `O(n r [T_Path+ell_max(T_step+T_Z)])` bit operations for the sparse template; the complete cloud has the analogous bound with its raw length `M`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: There are exactly `rn` core entries. Each uses one indexed descriptor, at most `ell_max` explicit steps, and one XOR per visited base entry. If all access times and `ell_max` are `n^{O(1)}` and `r≤n`, the full matrix is streamed in `n^{O(1)}` time. This is a conditional emitter lemma; no target-meeting `Path` is supplied.

proof_markdown:
## Scope

This is a certificate obstruction, not a universal upper bound on expander codes.

## 1. Normalization and all-one augmentation

For a binary word `c`, put `S(c)=n−2 wt(c)`. The target is met whenever `|S(c)|≤T=2^21`, equivalently normalized absolute bias at most `tau=1/512`. Such a balanced core `B` has every nonzero weight in `[D,n−D]` and cannot contain `1^n`. Hence `B⊕<1^n>` has dimension `dim(B)+1` and minimum distance at least `D`. Thus a balanced core of rank 1040 would already produce a k=1041 improvement.

Every parity-walk column is an XOR of outer labels, so amplification cannot increase their span.

For an undirected `d`-regular rotation multigraph on `m` vertices, write its normalized adjacency as `P_uv=a_uv/d` with integral symmetric port multiplicities. Then

`tr(P^2)=d^-2 Σ_uv a_uv^2 ≥ m/d`.

If every nonprincipal eigenvalue has absolute value at most `lambda`, then `tr(P^2)≤1+(m−1)lambda^2`. Therefore

`lambda^2 ≥ (m−d)/(d(m−1))`.  (1)

Blind adjustment of a raw absolute-bias bound `B_0M` gives `B_0M+|n−M|`. Even with `B_0=0`, puncturing requires

`M≤W=n+T=2^30+2^21=1,075,838,976`.  (2)

## 2. Complete s-wide amplification has balanced rank at most 64

For [Ta-Shma's Theorem 4.1](https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~amnon/Papers/T.STOC17.pdf), the complete cloud has

`M=N_1D_1^sD_2^t`

and certificate `Q^floor(t/s)`, where

`Q=lambda_2^s+s lambda_2^(s−1)+s^2(lambda_2^(s−3)+zeta)`

under `epsilon_0+2 beta+2 lambda_1≤lambda_2^2`.

A subunit certificate requires `t≥s`, `s≥4`, and `Q<1`. Indeed, `t<s` makes the exponent zero, while for `s≤3` a displayed term is at least one. From `Q<1`,

`s^2 lambda_2^(s−3)<1`,

so compatibility implies

`lambda_1^2 < a_s := (1/4)s^(−8/(s−3))`.  (3)

Assume the outer-label span has rank at least 65, hence `N_1≥65`. For `s=4,…,11`, let

`d_s=(65,64,58,50,42,36,31,27)`.

If `D_1≤d_s−1`, (1), minimized at `N_1=65`, gives respectively

`b_s=(1/4096,1/2016,1/456,1/196,3/328,3/224,7/384,3/128)`.

The exact rational quantities `(4b_s)^(s−3)s^8` are

`64, 390625/254016, 1679616/1481544, 1, 4076863488/3707398432, 31381059609/30840979456, 82354300000000/75144747810816, 1406408618241/1099511627776`,

all at least one. Thus `b_s≥a_s`, contradicting (3), and `D_1≥d_s`. Direct evaluation gives `65d_s^s≥65^5=1,160,290,625` throughout these cases.

For `s≥12`, (3) gives `lambda_1^2<1/4`. If `D_1≤3`, (1) gives `lambda_1^2≥(65−3)/(3·64)=31/96>1/4`. Hence `D_1≥4`, and

`M≥65·4^12=2^30+2^24=1,090,519,040`.  (4)

This is also below neither exact length nor the generic window (2), since `2^24>2^21`.

If `lambda_2=0`, compatibility forces `epsilon_0=beta=lambda_1=0`. The base multiset is then zero-biased; Fourier inversion makes it uniform on its ambient binary space, so rank at least 65 already forces at least `2^65` base entries. Thus zero creates no omitted case.

Consequently the published complete-output certificate has balanced rank at most 64 and reaches at most dimension 65 after standard all-one augmentation.

## 3. Ordinary complete walks also cannot challenge k=1040

Ta-Shma Theorem 3.1 gives support `M=m d^t` and certificate

`rho^floor(t/2)`, where `rho=epsilon_0+2 beta+2 lambda≥2lambda`.

Assume balanced-core rank at least 1040, so `m≥1040`, and `M≤W`. If `d=1`, (1) gives `lambda=1`. Otherwise `d≥2`, so `t≤19`.

For `t=2,3`, exact length gives `d≤1017`; (1) gives

`lambda^2≥23/(1017·1039)>1/2^16`,

so `rho>1/128>1/512`. For `4≤t≤9`, length gives `d≤31`; hence `lambda>1/6`, `rho>1/3`, and with `floor(t/2)≤4` the certificate is either at least one or greater than `(1/3)^4=1/81`. For `10≤t≤19`, length gives `d≤3`; then `lambda^2≥1037/(3·1039)>1/4`, so `rho>1`. The cases `t≤1` have exponent zero. No case certifies the target.

The paper's actual fallback is much worse: at `epsilon=1/512` it requires at least 64 steps. Its near-optimal Section 5 branch requires `alpha^3/(2log_2(1/alpha))≥1/9` with `alpha≤0.01`, whereas the left side is below `7.53·10^-8`.

## 4. The natural one-edge loophole has rank at most 899

Consider all directed ports of a symmetric `d`-regular graph, raw length `M=md`, and the standard scalar certificate

`beta=epsilon^2+lambda(1−epsilon^2)`.

Generic adjustment requires `beta M+|n−M|≤T`. The right-hand ratio is maximized at `M=n`, so `beta≤T/n=1/512`. Thus `lambda≤1/512` and every nonprincipal translated-label character sum `W_a` satisfies `|W_a|≤m/sqrt(512)`.

Equation (1) yields

`d≥ceil(262144m/(m+262143))`.

Together with `md≤W`, monotonicity and the exact boundary

`34915·30812≤W<34916·30813`

give `m≤34915`.

Let `h` be the translated-label span, equal to the edge-label span because `lambda<1` makes the graph connected. Fourier orthogonality at moment 200 gives

`Σ_a W_a^200=2^h Z_200`.

Counting tuples using 100 distinct indices twice gives

`Z_200≥L=(m)_100·199!!`.

Put `X=m^200/512^100`. Since

`199!!=100! binom(200,100)/2^100 ≥ (200/e)^100/201`,

we obtain

`L/X ≥ (1/201)[(200/e)·512(m−99)/m^2]^100`.

For `100≤m≤34915`, the bracket is minimized at `m=34915`; using `e<68/25`, it exceeds `43/40`. Since `(43/40)^10>2`, this gives `L>2X`. On the other hand,

`2^hL≤m^200+(2^h−1)X`,

so `2^h(L−X)<m^200`. As `L−X>X`,

`2^h<512^100=2^900`,

and therefore `h≤899`. The augmented dimension is at most 900.

## 5. Exact sparse-path handoff

The accepted k=1040 one-sided code contains an all-one codeword. For its corresponding message `x_0`, every base label satisfies `<x_0,Z(v)>=1`. Every fixed-length path therefore gives

`<x_0,g_q>=t+1 mod 2`,

so that direction becomes either zero, losing rank, or all-one, retaining absolute bias one. Starting from its genuine rank-1039 balanced core and augmenting afterward merely returns k=1040.

A competitive expander construction must therefore use a different rank-1040 balanced base or an explicitly indexed sparse family with mixed parity and a fresh simultaneous character-sum proof. Ta-Shma's full-cloud theorem does not survive thinning, deduplication, or nonuniform weighting automatically.

research_direction: Ta-Shma-style epsilon-balanced codes: exact finite complete-cloud ceilings and the sparse-path frontier.
theorem_statement: At `n=2^30` and absolute-bias target `1/512`, every complete-output instance certified by Ta-Shma's Theorem 4.1 has balanced rank at most 64; after the standard all-one augmentation it has dimension at most 65. The lower bound `2^30+2^24` on any contracting rank-at-least-65 cloud also exceeds the entire blind-puncturing window `2^30+2^21`. Ta-Shma's ordinary complete-walk certificate cannot support a rank-1040 balanced core, and the natural complete one-edge scalar spectral certificate has homogeneous rank at most 899. These are complete-cloud certificate obstructions, not a prohibition on a new explicitly indexed sparse or one-sided path construction.
title: Rank-64 ceiling for complete Ta-Shma amplification and an exact sparse-path handoff
